segments.text: This person has expressed that they want an app to track where new hires are in the onboarding process. Maybe they have sufficiently analyzed what's happening to know this is the right solution. However, very often, they haven't. Instead, maybe they decided to build an app because they like new apps, or because their colleague at another organization just built one, or maybe they do know that the onboarding process isn't smooth and they assume an app will make it better. In this situation, someone is naming what should be built rather than what should be different. They are assuming an answer before anyone has determined what the question is.

segments.text: We need an app to track where new hires are.
Why?
So managers can see who is stuck.
Why does that matter?
Because people sit for days waiting on something and nobody notices.
Why does that matter?
Because new hires should be contributing to their teams as quickly as possible, and right now they are not.
